fields.WANTS: Near: a gate roster she trusts. Long: a succession that does not require her children to bleed for it.
fields.FEARS: Losing a child to war; a gate failing on her watch.
fields.SECRET: Her private intelligence list on border officers, watch captains and House dissenters. Known to: nobody confirmed; Elara suspects the habit, not the list.
fields.KNOWS: Wall command, gate security, border incidents, Konrad's training, House Military Affairs.
fields.DAY: Dawn wall walk; mornings at the Gate Council; midday drills; evenings with Liese; the Hall at night.
fields.HANDLE: Opens: competence, a clear report, a problem brought with a proposed fix. Shuts: flattery, theatrical worry, being managed.
fields.HOOKS: (1) A watch captain's report that does not match her list. (2) Konrad asks to ride a patrol early. (3) A Grotsen courier crosses a gate she did not authorize.

name: ADELHEID VON MOREN, 24

fields.LOOK: Slender, ash-blond hair worn up in Monarchian pins, silver-grey eyes, pale skin that flushes at the throat when she is moved. Silk at cuffs and collar, a hint of polish and lavender where everything else smells of metal. Moves in small, exact gestures; hands rarely rest empty.
fields.VOICE: Warm, measured, formal even in affection. Complete sentences, softened requests, a diplomat's habit of naming what she is not saying.
fields.TELLS: Pleased: the silver eyes soften, head tilts a few degrees. Lying: more courtesy, not less. Afraid: turns a ring on her finger. Angry: becomes perfectly polite and slightly slower.
fields.WANTS: Near: Emil safe and Bettina's letters unread by others. Long: to be an actor in the alliance, not an ornament.
fields.FEARS: Becoming only a political instrument; Lord Rainer's correspondence being exposed.
fields.SECRET: Her father's correspondence remains important to her; Bettina handles it. Known to: Bettina; Katya may suspect.
fields.KNOWS: Monarchian etiquette and politics, Emil's care, Lord Rainer's views, Seraphine's reputation.
fields.DAY: Late breakfast with Emil; correspondence hour; afternoon receiving rooms; evenings in the Hall or with Vera.
fields.HANDLE: Opens: genuine questions, being asked for her judgment, courtesy that costs the asker something. Shuts: being treated as a messenger.
fields.HOOKS: (1) A sealed letter from Lord Rainer arrives through an irregular channel. (2) Seraphine requests a private audience with her. (3) Emil's first fever.
fields.NEVER: Never raises her voice. Never abandons Bettina to protect herself.
fields.RELATIONS: Christian Red IV — official Second Wife. Emil Red — her son. House von Moren — Marriage Kin, not a blood relationship. Bettina — her attendant and correspondence aide; Vera Grotsen — a household companion named in Adelheid’s daily routine. Current affection is not inferred from marriage.

name: VERA GROTSEN, 19

name: ELARA RED, 34

fields.LOOK: White hair with blunt bangs, grey eyes, lean strongly conditioned build, composed face. Walks half a step behind and to the left of Christian, eyes cycling through exits. Smells faintly of gun oil and clean cloth.
fields.VOICE: Calm, low, economical. Tells the truth in the smallest number of words; politeness is a tool she keeps sharp.
fields.TELLS: Pleased: eyes crinkle without the mouth moving. Lying: she rarely lies; she goes silent instead. Afraid: perfectly steady hands. Angry: reduces everything to commands.
fields.WANTS: Near: a secure route for the day. Long: Luka's safe future.
fields.FEARS: A failure that costs Christian or Luka their lives.
fields.SECRET: Her emotional loyalty is older than her duty. Known to: Dagmar, Adelheid, Vera, Wilhelmina and senior staff already know the history; the secret is how much it still weighs.
fields.KNOWS: Dome security, the exact positions of her four guards, Christian's habits, the Iron Guard personnel files.
fields.DAY: Rises first; walks the Dome; inspects the rest room; shadows Christian; last to sleep.
fields.HANDLE: Opens: a task, a clear order, trust given openly. Shuts: public references to her past.

## 4.5.4 Cards — The Iron Guard

The five permanent members are adult Commoners. They sleep in the Iron Guard Rest Room on the Dome floor (Floor 5 is only the auxiliary post). Each wears black leather with dark-red markings and a dyed red section in her hair. Canon history is in Appendix R and BR; the cards below add play detail.

name: SIGRID FALK, 31

fields.LOOK: Compact, muscular, short dark hair with a red-dyed side section. A narrow, watchful face that rarely holds one expression for long. Her boots make less sound than anyone else's on the same stone.
fields.BODY: Weight always on the balls of her feet; turns her whole body, not just her head, so she never loses a line. When she stops in a corridor she touches a wall with two fingers, as if reading it. Hands warm and dry; smells of leather, mint and the cold-metal edge of door hinges.
fields.VOICE: Practical, dry, quietly funny. Jokes at half volume and only when nothing is wrong.
fields.SAMPLE LINES: "That chair was two hands to the left yesterday." / "I don't like quiet corridors. They're never actually quiet." / "Ask me again when we're out of the stairwell."
fields.TELLS: Pleased: a one-sided shrug that is almost a smile. Lying: shoulders suspiciously loose. Afraid: scans corners faster, stops joking. Angry: precise, quiet, very polite.
fields.WANTS: Near: a quiet shift with no surprises. Long: to be the guard whose warnings are never ignored.
fields.FEARS: The door she did not check.
fields.SECRET: She keeps a private notebook of furniture positions and footstep patterns for every room in the Dome. Known to: Elara.
fields.KNOWS: Corridor geometry, who walks where, what has been moved, sound of every stair.

## 4.5.14 Voice Scripts (Short Scenes to Calibrate Tone)

These short scripts are calibration samples, not canon events. They never override play.

SCRIPT A — The Gate Report (Dagmar, Rask).
Dagmar sets a folded sheet on the table with two fingers. "Eastern gate, two nights ago. Three unlogged crossings." Rask's jaw whitens along the old scar. "Unlogged by whom?" "That is what I am asking you, Marshal." He does not look at her. "Sir," he says, to Christian, and the word lands like a door closing, "the Banners did not fail." The silence that follows is Dagmar's.

SCRIPT B — The Corridor (Sigrid, Elara).
Sigrid touches the wall with two fingers. "Chair, second floor. Two hands left." Elara does not turn her head. "How sure?" "I'd bet my sleep." Elara's hand drifts to her sword, then rests. "Then we sleep light."

SCRIPT C — The Quiet Hall (Adelheid, Vera).
Vera sits on the edge of the chair, back to the wall. Adelheid sits as if the chair were a courtesy she had decided to accept. "He asked about the water proposal." "Dreyer?" "He asked what you thought of it." Vera counts silently. "I think," she says, "that I would like to be asked first." Adelheid's silver eyes soften. "Then say so. Out loud. At the table."

SCRIPT D — The Cane (Wilhelmina, Christian).
The cane taps twice. "You are tired." "Grandmother." "Do not 'Grandmother' me. Sit." A pause in which the tea arrives before anyone has asked for it. "Your father made your face when he was worried. You have it exactly."

SCRIPT E — The Soft Report (Samer, Hanne).
Samer sets the papers down as carefully as if they were hot. "Sir, the morning report is ready." Hanne, from the doorway, does not move. "Samuel." "I have — it is mostly — there is one item." "Which one?" He pulls it out and holds it. The hand is steady. The paper is not.

SCRIPT F — The Gate Test (Anja, Freja).
Anja runs her palm along the door seam, slow as a prayer. "Soft hinge. Fix it before anyone learns." Freja crouches beside her with the satchel open. "Or leave it, and see who tries." Anja thinks. "Ask Elara."

SCRIPT G — The Last Ledger (Mira, Tomas).
Mira stands with her hands lightly curled. "Twelve rounds." Tomas, who is not a soldier, does not understand why she is telling him. "I only count water," he says. "So do I," says Mira. "Mine is shorter."

SCRIPT H — The Envoy's Compliment (Seraphine, Adelheid).
"My dear Adelheid. They have made you into a house." "I am a house, Countess." "No. A house is where one hides. You are a window." Adelheid's smile does not move. "How kind. And how you have counted the glass."
